newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM to dissolve house, call election - deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM to dissolve house, call election - deputy PM.

text.p: Thailand's outgoing premier Banharn Silpa-archa will dissolve parlaiment and call a snap election on November 17, Deputy Prime Minister Samak Sundaravej said on Friday.
The surprise decision, conveyed by Samak, a close ally of the premier, angered some coalition partners who had expected Banharn to name a successor and leave the coalition intact.
Samak told reporters that Banharn, who leads a six-party coalition government that controls 209 of the 391 seats in parliament, would make an announcement later.
Samak said Banharn had decided to dissolve the house because there was no full agreement among members of his coalition on the choice of a replacement.
Banharn last Saturday was forced by his allies to declare he would quit within seven days, and had kept the nation and his coalition allies in the dark over his replacement for six days.
"There was a deadlock on the choice (of a new prime minister)," Samak said after coalition leaders met with Banharn.

The announcement shocked supporters of Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, leader of the New Aspiration Party, the second largest party in the coalition. Chavalit had been seen as front-runner for the premiership.
But Chavalit failed to get the nomination after losing support from key members of Banharn's core Chart Thai party, which has 91 seats, coalition sources said.
There was no immediate comment from Chavalit.
"It (the decision) surprised me because he had promised that he would not dissolve the house," said Foreign Minister Amnuay Viravan, who is also in charge of economic affairs in the administration.
Another coalition leader, Chalerm Yoobumroong, who heads the small Muon Chon party, said Banharn made the decision without consulting coalition partners.
"He solely made the decision, so he has to explain to the people why he did not keep his word," he said.
A royal proclamation on holding a fresh election was expected later, government sources said.
